title: fix(app-shell): the Studio decides a screen field's visibleWhen live, through the runner's renderer, over the screen's declared fields (objectui#10743)
body:
Fixes #10743
Clause-②: no — the Studio's screen preview and Debug run rebind to the runner's own evaluator; no export on `@object-ui/app-shell`'s index, no spec shape and no accept set moves (`screen-spec.ts` and `ScreenView`'s scope helper are module-internal)

Executes the seat's ruling on objectui#10743 (comment 5853038135, option C: one contract, one scope) with the amended claim 5852879659. The server half is objectstack-ai/objectstack#20178 and does not block this. The flow runner (`ScreenView`, `FlowRunner`) has NO behaviour change; `ScreenView` only exports its existing `screenPredicateScope`.

## What changed

- `screen-spec.ts` — `buildScreenSpec(node)` keeps every authored field and carries its `visibleWhen` raw, as the runtime `screen` executor sends it to the client; it no longer takes `variables` and no longer decides visibility. `ScreenView` decides it live, over the screen's declared fields and the values the author collects in the preview — the one client evaluator. The Studio's own evaluator for this key is removed: `isFieldVisibleWhen`, `fieldVisibility`, and the simulator's `evalVisibleWhen` (`flow-sim-validate.ts`; `evalCelPredicate` keeps serving edge guards and decision branches).
- `unevaluableVisibleWhen(node)` judges SCOPE, never value: a field whose predicate references a root that is not a field declared on this screen (a run variable such as `needsApproval`, the runtime's `vars` root), does not parse as CEL (a `{var}` brace), or is a shape `registerFlow` refuses, is named with the reason and the nearest declared field for a typo. The roots come from `collectCelRootIdentifiers` (`@objectstack/formula` 17.4.0) checked against `Object.keys(screenPredicateScope(spec, {}))` plus `record`, the namespace `ScreenView` binds the same values under — read off the renderer, not restated. A sibling-field predicate (`discount` above zero, `record.discount`) is not reported.
- `hiddenFieldCount(spec, values)` is the renderer's own verdict (`screenFields` minus `visibleScreenFields`), so the preview's "N fields hidden by their visible when condition" hint follows every tick and keystroke; it moved into `ScreenFormPreview`, where the values live.
- `flow-simulator.ts` — the screen pause records the scope findings on the step's `error` (the panel draws it in rose), and the note is the plain "Screen reached — provide inputs, then continue." A run with such a field still pauses: `registerFlow` on objectstack main does not refuse it yet (that is objectstack#20178).
- `ScreenPreview.tsx` — `variables` now feed `{var}` interpolation only; the docblock says so.
- Published text rewritten wherever it said the Studio takes "the runtime's resume-door reading": `screen-spec.ts`, `ScreenPreview.tsx`, `flow-simulator.ts`, `flow-sim-validate.ts`, `packages/app-shell/README.md`, and the pending `.changeset/10692-debug-run-routing-parity.md` (a dated note in the objectui#10533 form; its frontmatter is untouched). Each states that the server's resume door still reads the run's variables until objectstack#20178 lands. No server behaviour that is not on objectstack main is claimed.
- One changeset, `.changeset/10743-studio-screen-visiblewhen-live.md`, `'@object-ui/app-shell': patch`.

## H1 — the paused-run payload carries no run variables (both sides, from source)

- objectstack `service-automation` `engine.ts`, the screen-pause arm of `execute` and of `resumeInternal`: `return { success: true, status: 'paused', runId, durationMs, screen: err.screen };` — no variables member; the subflow re-pause arm is the same shape with `childRes.screen`.
- spec `contracts/automation-service.ts` `AutomationResult` members: success, output, error, durationMs, code, status, runId, screen, successMessage, errorMessage, refusalMessage, summary — no variables. `ScreenSpec` members: nodeId, title, description, fields, kind, objectName, mode, recordId, defaults, idVariable.
- runtime `domains/automation.ts`: the trigger door serves the engine result verbatim, `if (isPausedRun(result)) { return { handled: true, response: deps.success(result) }; }`; the resume door likewise after `automationService.resume(parts[2], signal)`; the screen door answers `deps.success({ runId: parts[2], screen })`.
- The one door that discloses `variables` for a paused run is GET runs/RUN_ID (an `ExecutionLogEntry`, objectstack#7639), behind `isRunStateRead` and `refuseUngrantedRunRead` (the sys_automation_run read grant); its own comment: applying the grant to the screen route "would lock out the end user the flow paused for".
- objectui: `interpretFlowResponse`'s paused arm carries `{ kind: 'paused', runId, screen, data }`, `judgeFlowLaunch` forwards `{ kind: 'screen', runId, screen }`, `FlowRunner`'s `ScreenFlowState` is `{ flowName, runId, screen }`. Nothing is received and dropped.

## H2 — producers

- No shipped flow authors a screen `visibleWhen` over a run variable, in either repo. objectstack example flows with screen nodes: `examples/app-crm` `convert-lead.flow.ts` (a waitForInput message screen and two object-form screens, no `visibleWhen`), `examples/app-showcase` `showcase_reassign_wizard` (one flat field, no `visibleWhen`), `examples/app-todo` `task.flow.ts` (`visibleWhen` appears only in a comment).
- Every measured screen `visibleWhen` predicates over a sibling field: the flows guide (`opportunityName`, `createOpportunity == true`), the console preview sample (`note`, `discount` above zero), and the objectstack and lint test fixtures.

## H3 — the ruling, and what the Studio was doing (M1, M2, measured on the base)

Option C: a screen field's `visibleWhen` binds the same screen's declared fields plus the values being collected — the spec `ScreenFieldSpec.visibleWhen` docblock ("Bare CEL over the screen's own field names", "evaluated by the CLIENT … not by the server"). The runner already implements it; the Studio, since PR objectui#10736, read the resume door instead. Measured with the real `FlowSimulator` and `ScreenPreview` on the base `704e05b09d` (probe file, not committed):

- M1 console sample: at the pause `note` is absent (`buildScreenSpec` dropped it; the step note read "Hidden because its visibleWhen could not be evaluated … Unknown variable: discount"); typing `5` into Discount leaves `note` absent; the control `comment` is drawn throughout. Docs shape: `opportunityName` absent; ticking the checkbox (`data-state` goes to checked) leaves it absent; control `plain` drawn. With the flow variable declared `false` in the run (as the guide recommends): the predicate evaluated `false`, the field was dropped, the tick changed nothing. ⇒ frozen, exactly the outcome the runtime's `screen` executor forwards the predicate raw to avoid.
- M2 `unevaluableVisibleWhen` over the run's variables named the sibling predicates (`note`, `opportunityName`) as unevaluable, and did NOT name a genuine run-variable predicate when the run held the variable (`needsApproval: true` → nothing reported); with `needsApproval: false` seeded, `reason` was hidden silently.
- Toolchain facts the fix rests on: `@objectstack/formula` 17.4.0 exports `collectCelRootIdentifiers` and `nearestName`; on the runner's seeded scope, `createOpportunity == true` with `false` evaluates `false`, and `discount` above zero with `null` faults ("no such overload"), which `ScreenView`'s fallback then decides — its direction (objectui#8069), not this card's.

## Pins — red on the base, green on the head, each with a control in the same tree

Files: `ScreenPreview.debugRunScope-10743.test.tsx` (new; real `FlowSimulator` → real `ScreenPreview`, mounted as the panel mounts them), `ScreenPreview.test.tsx` (re-judged), `simulator/__tests__/flow-simulator.parity-10692.test.ts` (re-judged).

- the sibling-field predicate reveals its field live: console sample (`5` reveals `note`, `0` hides it; `comment` drawn throughout), docs shape (tick reveals `opportunityName`; `plain` drawn throughout; hint appears then goes), docs shape with the flow variable seeded `false`;
- a run-variable predicate is not read from the run's variables: the render is the same whether the run holds `needsApproval` `true` or `false` (`plain` drawn in both), and the screen step names `"reason"` with `needsApproval` as an error whatever the run holds; the sibling pause carries no error and names no field;
- `unevaluableVisibleWhen`: sibling, `record.` sibling, two siblings, no predicate, blank → not reported; run variable, stdlib call over a run variable, `vars` root, brace, non-string → reported by field name; typo → nearest declared field named;
- `buildScreenSpec` keeps every field with its `visibleWhen`; `hiddenFieldCount(spec, values)` reads 1 then 0.

Red leg (committed head tests over the base sources `704e05b09d`, five source files checked out from BASE, restored with `git checkout HEAD --` and blob hashes re-checked against HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty): `Tests 24 failed | 35 passed (59)`, all three files red; the 35 passes are the controls and the pre-existing cases. Green leg at `39fbfac155`, seven files (the three above plus `flow-simulator.test.ts`, `FlowSimulatorPanel.test.tsx`, `spec-symbol-parity.test.ts`, `ScreenView.requiredMarker-10367.test.tsx`): `Test Files 7 passed (7)`, `Tests 138 passed (138)`.

Ablations (each through `ablation-replace.mjs` in wrap mode: anchor hit exactly once, blob changed, tests run, restored with blob equal to HEAD and `git diff HEAD` empty):

- A1 `toScreenFields` stops carrying `visibleWhen` → 8 red (the live-reveal pins, `keeps every field` in both files);
- A2 `hiddenFieldCount` returns 0 → 3 red (the two hint pins, the count pin);
- A3 the undeclared-roots filter yields nothing → 8 red (run-variable and `vars` rows in both files, the typo pin, the step-error pin; brace and non-string stay reported by the parse and shape legs);
- A4 the simulator no longer asks `unevaluableVisibleWhen` → 6 red (every step-error row, the debug-run step pin);
- A5 the hint never renders → 2 red (both hint pins);
- A6 the roots ignore `screenPredicateScope` and keep only `record` → 5 red (sibling not-reported rows, the sibling pause row, the two live-reveal debug-run pins whose steps now carry an error).

## Gates (at `39fbfac155`)

- Dependency closure `turbo run build --filter='@object-ui/app-shell^...' --concurrency=2` under the verify lock: `Tasks: 28 successful, 28 total`, `VERDICT command-exit 0`.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check` (script echoed `@object-ui/app-shell@17.6.0 type-check`, `tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`): exit 0; `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFiles` lists the new pin file (1).
- eslint on the eight changed source/test files: 0 errors (12 pre-existing warnings in `ScreenView.tsx`, react-refresh and no-explicit-any, untouched lines).
- `check-changeset-presence` ✅ (7 published source files, 1 changeset declared); `check-control-bytes` ✅; `check-vi-mock-specifiers` ✅; `check-vi-mock-override-shape` ✅; `check-test-path-roots` ✅; `check-pending-changeset-literals` ✅; `check-changeset-claims` ✅ (report-only, no pending body names a touched file); `check-new-line-citations`: `VERDICT 0 new citation(s)`.
- NOT MEASURED locally: `check-readme-exports` — exit 1 on a prerequisite (app-shell `dist/index.d.ts` absent, "run pnpm build first", 8 packages unbuilt); the README edit is prose and adds no fenced import block. The repo-level `pnpm lint` and full `pnpm test` are CI's runs.

## Serial

Claim time 05:28Z: no open PR touched `metadata-admin/previews/`, `ScreenView.tsx` or `FlowRunner.tsx`. Re-checked before the final push (12 open PRs, file lists read by REST): none touches those paths (the release PR objectui#5400 lists release artefacts on its first page of 100 files). `origin/main` fetched into the private ref `refs/issue-10743/main` = `704e05b09d` = this branch's base; `git merge-tree --write-tree` exit 0; no commit on main since the base touches a file this PR changes. No merge commit was needed.

## Acceptance notes

- Direction, unchanged and out of scope (objectui#8069): under `ScreenView`'s fallback the console sample's `note` is drawn before any discount is typed — `discount` is seeded `null`, the comparison faults in CEL, and `evalFieldPredicate` falls open — and hides once `0` is typed. The pins read the live decision after typing, not the initial fallback.
- The flow node inspector's `visibleWhen` placeholder (`inspectors/flow-node-config.ts`) reads `stage == "review"`, a run-variable-shaped example on a screen field; under this ruling it invites a predicate the renderer cannot evaluate and objectstack#20178 will refuse at `registerFlow`. Noted, not filed here (outside the claimed surface).
- The screen step's error text is an English literal like its neighbouring step notes (the simulator's notes are not in the i18n catalogue).
- Object-form screens are untouched (`screenFields` is empty for them); `interpolate` and the `{var}` title/description path are untouched.
- The retired Studio functions were never on `@object-ui/app-shell`'s index; the `ScreenView` export is additive and module-level only.
- The runtime's resume door still evaluates over the run's variables until objectstack#20178 lands: until then a run-variable predicate is an error in the Studio, shown by the runner, and its `required` waived by the server.
